I was once just asking for a single page webapp once. I mentioned it's for Japanese users and Gemini started to completely destroy the HTML, trying to turn it into a typical mile-long receipt style page.

LLMs are still text completion engines, Maybe in the way we humans are merely adaptable to spacewalks and not designed to do it, but I think wild claims like "China backdoors LLM to generate vulnerabilities for dissents" needs more substantiation than just these random experiments.

> For China, the political restrictions are applied at the presentation/UI layer only

“…when telling DeepSeek-R1 that it was coding for an industrial control system based in Tibet, the likelihood of it generating code with severe vulnerabilities increased to 27.2%. This was an increase of almost 50% compared to the baseline” [1].

> there is no law that restricts releasing open models that are capable of producing “wrongthink” output

“…several open-source datasets were ‘dealt with’, using the official language, despite the fact that open weights distributed for free are not subject to most of the Chinese AI regulations” [2]. That soft guidance likely goes hard with the mooted “comprehensive AI legislation” [3].

[1] https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-researche...

[2] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/TKcjrvcMuY7Ca7Ya9/china-ai-s...

[3] https://intelligence.dlapiper.com/artificial-intelligence/?t...

The reasons behind the Chinese models’ refusals to talk about politically sensitive topics and western models’ “alignment” are different.

For China, the political restrictions are applied at the presentation/UI layer only to comply with the law. I’m pretty sure there is no law that restricts releasing open models that are capable of producing “wrongthink” output (in this case, an RNG would technically also be off limits since it could produce the wrong output given enough time). This can be effectively implemented by a “neutral” model with a smaller, “review” model being used to censor replies rather than “aligning” the initial model itself to be politically correct.

In contrast, Western labs’ “alignment” strategy is a PR move, meaning they want the refusals to be loud and clear (as opposed to being merely an inconvenient law they have to comply with), to support the idea that their models are so powerful and would mean doom if they weren’t “aligned”.

children.text: The panpsychism fad seems like late Millennials'/Gen Z's cope with death. My greater point is that the same way you "are" your kidney today (or how you "are" the nearest mushroom, or microchip) is the same way you will be those things when you're dead: Utterly unnoticable, aka not at all. Not to mention that your memories will be wiped and that's not even controversial to a panpsychist. The problem is that panpsychists assert consciousness as something independent of memories, which is an indefensible position imo. A memory-less stream of impressions would be equivalent to death. Every moment would be your first, totally disconnected from all else, just to instantly vanish, never to be processed. That's the opposite of consciousness. Some kind of memory feedback/storage/processing is needed. And your ability to generate that lies in the shape of your brain, where it doesn't matter which electrons flow through it - you're not the specific electrons.

I don't know, we don't communicate in a way that I could ask it.

But the principles of biological organization are often fractal. If you observe a phenomenon at one level (selection acting on an organism, say) you can often zoom out and see it again (acting at the ecosystem level) or you can zoom in and see it (at the organ level, the tissue level, or even on certain macromolecules).

It's not necessary for me to be able to strike up a conversation with my kidney for me to see that it's well situated to experience changes in my diet a bit like how we experience el nino, the machinations of my immune system might be like politics to it. I'll never know for sure, so I err on the side of caution.

What is it like to be your left kidney? Your brain is connected to it through nerves, which ofc are conscious too in your worldview. If fungus and rocks are consciously linked, there should be a conscious link between your brain and your kidney. Yet, you have no idea what your kidney is experiencing every day, it certainly doesn't have any deep thoughts. And when the kidney gets taken out of your body, your conscious experience won't change. When your brain gets surgically or violently altered on the other hand...

children.author: recursive

children.text:
When I think about the experience that these AI models have, I often wonder if they know that we exist. I mean, it took us a very long time to discover mitochondria, despite the fact that we like... live together and work out together and eat together and die together. When the first eukaryotic cells formed, the mitochondria probably thought they were in charge too--just like we think we're in charge.

I just pointed it out because I wanted to dodge the same old AI debates. They're very narrow. Like, people have been arguing about whether general intelligence exists for decades, and now that some VC wants to use AGI as a buzzword, we ignore that GI is not a settled issue. And consciousness... golly that's like THE intractable philosophical problem. It's a bottomless pit. Ain't nobody knows what they're talking about when it comes to consciousness.

I'm sympathetic to the reflex: this guy has beliefs that he doesn't realize are dangerous. Let's help him. I'm usually on the opposite side of this one. I just think we need to find ways to address the potential harms without actually winning a debate about consciousness. Beliefs about it are too varied and too tightly held. People don't win debates about consciousness. If they work super hard maybe they get a tenured position as a philosopher so they can continue the debate, but they never win.

Interesting approach. I hadn't heard of it. I think treating rocks and fungus and trees with empathy is a different kind of thing and safer than an LLM.

I've been a panpsychist for a while now. I think that trees and fungus and rocks are conscious. It has not yet manifested as attack surface, so far as I'm aware.

But if I were to practice indifference, I think that would have a negative effect immediately.
Your empathy towards the machine controlled by the trillion dollar conglomerate is a vulnerability and will one day be used against you.

children.author: arbol
Xirdus
children.text: Per the article, "Astra was not willing to comply with the request. I also attempted this using the Daybreak Blue toggle with the same result, blocked."

This stuff doesn't work. The agents read the AST and just ignore dead code. Even replacing all your function names at build time with decoys makes the agent see the juxtaposition.

You need evil context as well as evil names, and then you need to run the evil code! Not an appropriate defense on client sites.

To stop deobfuscation at scale, you're better off serving so many bundles that mass scraping can't scale, as they cannot reliably deobfuscate your code. This forces them into the browser and it's behavioural analysis from this point onwards.

children.text: LLMs are not training on obfuscated fingerprinting scripts, and there’s essentially no way that could become associated with your brand.

A customer might want to prevent LLMs parsing or executing code on the site for a range of reasons. But their intent might not be for the LLM or model provider to see content like that on the site, on the company domain, alongside the brand and assets. And unless the customer reverses what the Russian company is doing, they have no idea about the content their brand is feeding a model provider.

For example, let’s say I decided to use their anti-fraud system which prevents attackers from using LLM automated attacks. I’ve been working hard to publish content that makes it clear to LLMs what we do and that we’re the best choice for a category of customers. Suddenly my brand is associated with cyberattacks, bioweapon development, financial mischief, poisons, and we’ve also taken an anti-China position on Tiananmen square.

The response a customer might get next time they ask about my company in an LLM chat could be quite interesting.
